correctness.rationale: For c>1, L=log c and h_a(t)=a^-1 exp(-t/a)1_(t>0), ψ_c=h_c-h_1 has squared norm N²=(c-1)²/[2c(c+1)]. Direct <h_a,h_b>=1/(a+b) expands to Gram g_k=2(c+1)² c^(3k/2)/[(c+c^k)(1+c^k)(1+c^(k+1))]. The unitary x=log t map converts L²-normalized dilates to translations by jL. The Mellin transform gives Gamma(1/2-iξ)(c^(-1/2-iξ)-1)/N, and |Gamma(1/2+iξ)|²=pi/cosh(pi ξ), producing the periodic positive Gram symbol G_c(theta)=pi(1+q²-2q cos theta)/(L N²) sum_m sech[pi(theta+2pi m)/L], q=c^-1/2. Its continuous positive minimum/maximum are sharp two-sided and one-sided Riesz bounds via Fejér concentration; positivity of all g_k gives maximum at 0. For L->0, the nearest two antipodal aliases give P_L(pi)~4 exp(-pi²/L), D_L(pi)/N²~16/L²; uniform two-range comparison excludes shifted smaller values and yields A~64pi L^-3 exp(-pi²/L), B~pi/L, B/A~L² exp(pi²/L)/64. Independent numerical Mellin symbol checks at L=.5,.3,.2 gave A_symbol(pi)/asymptotic ≈1.02606,1.00938,1.00417, while B_symbol(0)/asymptotic ≈1.01546,1.00560,1.00250. These finite numbers corroborate but do not prove infinite Gram and uniform minimization.
